"""Fresh test of the shared-floor picture of shear transfer (LESSONS 18; Opus, swarm S2 k44 front).

python scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py
Seen so far (k44_cofree Co set, blind by file timestamp only): the residual of the volume-transfer pair rule is the
same in both shears, so the anisotropy A = K44 - K' transfers as sum 4 x_i x_j A_ij(V0) and K44 transfers with k ~1
once e' = K' - rule' is a covariate. Here both are pre-registered in the ledger on 150 new random alloys (half with
Co >= 15%), drawn with a new seed and never computed. Targets use SQS seed 100: binaries use seeds 0-2, and compute.py:56
makes the site permutation depend only on (seed, n), so a shared seed leaks configuration noise (S2 audit, ledger
withdrawal of 9cfc8edaf0). Plain K44 per Co set is reported, not gated.
PASS needs all three: (1) A rule: RMSE <= 0.9 x pair-at-V_ij and sign-flip p < 0.005; (2) corr(e44, e') >= 0.5;
(3) joint fit K44 - pair44 = k T44 + b e': k and b both in [0.7, 1.3].
"""

import datetime as dt
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
import importlib.util  # noqa: E402

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402

from harness import ledger  # noqa: E402

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("kst", ROOT / "scripts" / "k_shear_transfer.py")
kst = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(kst)
from harness import compute  # noqa: E402
from harness.features import parse_comp  # noqa: E402

ctx, curvatures, test = kst.ctx, kst.curvatures, kst.test
g = kst.g.copy()
g["A"] = g.K44 - g.Kp
spl = {(tuple(k.split("-")), ch): kst.CubicSpline(s.dlnV, s[ch]) for k, s in g.groupby("pair") for ch in ("K44", "Kp", "A")}
OUT = ROOT / "data" / "k_aniso_s100_clamped.csv"
SCRIPT = str(Path(__file__))
CLAIM = "Shared shear floor, disjoint seeds"
ELS = ["Ag", "Au", "Co", "Cu", "Ir", "Ni", "Pd", "Pt", "Rh"]
N = 108

seen = set()
for f in ("a2_shear_clamped", "h3_shear_clamped", "hm_shear_clamped", "k44_cofree_clamped"):
    seen |= set(pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / f"{f}.csv").comp)
for f in ("h3_fresh_rows_fixed", "hm_fresh_rows_fixed"):
    seen |= set(pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / f"{f}.csv").comp_actual)


def draw(rng, with_co):
    while True:
        k = int(rng.integers(3, 6))
        pool = [e for e in ELS if e != "Co"]
        els = sorted(([*rng.choice(pool, k - 1, replace=False), "Co"]) if with_co else rng.choice(pool, k, replace=False))
        cnt = 11 + rng.multinomial(N - 11 * k, rng.dirichlet(np.ones(k)))
        c = {e: n / N for e, n in zip(els, cnt)}
        s = ";".join(f"{e}:{c[e]:.4f}" for e in sorted(c))
        if (not with_co or c["Co"] >= 0.15) and s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            return s, c


rng = np.random.default_rng(20261102)
comps = [draw(rng, i % 2 == 1) for i in range(150)]


def pr(c, ch, at):
    v = ctx.vegard(c)
    return sum(4 * xa * xb * float(spl[((a, b), ch)](np.log(v / ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"]) if at else 0.0))
               for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))


P = {ch: (np.array([pr(c, ch, 1) for _, c in comps]), np.array([pr(c, ch, 0) for _, c in comps])) for ch in ("K44", "Kp", "A")}


def judge(y44, yp):
    okA, gain, p = test(y44 - yp, *P["A"])
    e44, ep = y44 - P["K44"][0], yp - P["Kp"][0]
    r = float(np.corrcoef(e44, ep)[0, 1])
    k, b = np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[P["K44"][0] - P["K44"][1], ep], y44 - P["K44"][1], rcond=None)[0]
    return okA and r >= 0.5 and 0.7 <= k <= 1.3 and 0.7 <= b <= 1.3, gain, p, r, float(k), float(b)


# realistic noise, from the rows already computed (seen): K' residual of the rule, and the A residual on top of it
seenrows = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / f"{f}.csv") for f in ("h3_shear_clamped", "hm_shear_clamped", "k44_cofree_clamped")])
sc = [parse_comp(s) for s in seenrows.comp]
ep_s = seenrows.Kp.values - np.array([pr(c, "Kp", 1) for c in sc])
eA_s = (seenrows.K44 - seenrows.Kp).values - np.array([pr(c, "A", 1) for c in sc])
SP, SA = 1.2 * float(np.std(ep_s)), 1.2 * float(np.std(eA_s))  # x1.2: seen rows carry the seed leak
regs = [e for e in ledger.entries() if e["claim"].startswith(CLAIM) and "prereg" in e["notes"]]
if not regs:
    r2 = np.random.default_rng(4)

    def sim(truth):
        hits = []
        for i in range(300):
            ep = r2.normal(0, SP, len(comps))
            yp = P["Kp"][0] + ep
            y44 = (P["K44"][0] if truth == 0 else P["K44"][1]) + ep + r2.normal(0, SA, len(comps))
            if truth == 1:
                yp = P["Kp"][1] + ep
            hits.append(judge(y44, yp)[0])
        return float(np.mean(hits))

    power, fp = sim(0), sim(1)
    print(f"n {len(comps)}, sigma K' {SP:.2f}, sigma A {SA:.2f}, power {power:.3f}, false pass {fp:.3f}", flush=True)
    reg = ledger.register(f"{CLAIM}: in clamped random fcc alloys the volume-transfer pair rule misses a part common to "
                          f"K44 and K'; PASS if on {len(comps)} new random alloys (half Co >= 15%) (1) A = K44 - K' rule "
                          f"sum 4 x_i x_j A_ij(V0) has RMSE <= 0.9 x pair-at-V_ij and sign-flip p < 0.005, (2) "
                          f"corr(e44, e') >= 0.5, (3) joint fit K44 - pair44 = k T44 + b e' gives k, b in [0.7, 1.3]",
                          SCRIPT, {"power": power, "false_pass": fp},
                          notes="Opus swarm S2 k44 front; seen confirmation on k44_cofree Co set (LESSONS 18)")
    print("registered", reg["id"], flush=True)
    regs = [reg]

done = set(pd.read_csv(OUT)["comp"]) if OUT.exists() else set()
for s, c in comps:
    if s in done:
        continue
    alloy = compute.solid_solution(c, "fcc", reps=3, seed=100)
    x = compute.actual_fractions(alloy)
    r = {"comp": s, "n_el": len(c), "co": c.get("Co", 0.0), "V0": ctx.vegard(c), **curvatures(alloy, x, ctx.vegard(c)),
         "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    pd.DataFrame([r]).to_csv(OUT, mode="a", header=not OUT.exists(), index=False)
print("aniso targets done", flush=True)

t = pd.read_csv(OUT).set_index("comp").loc[[s for s, _ in comps]]
ok, gain, p, r, k, b = judge(t.K44.values, t.Kp.values)
print(f"A rule gain {gain:.2f}, p {p:.1e}; corr(e44, e') {r:.2f}; joint k {k:.2f}, b {b:.2f} -> {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}",
      flush=True)
for lab, m in (("Co-free", t.co.values == 0), ("Co", t.co.values > 0)):
    T, Y = (P["K44"][0] - P["K44"][1])[m], (t.K44.values - P["K44"][1])[m]
    _, gn, pp = test(t.K44.values[m], P["K44"][0][m], P["K44"][1][m])
    print(f"not gated, plain K44 {lab} (n {m.sum()}): gain {gn:.2f}, p {pp:.1e}, k {T @ Y / (T @ T):.2f}", flush=True)
ledger.record(f"{CLAIM}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'} on {len(comps)} new alloys (A gain {gain:.2f}, p {p:.1e}, corr {r:.2f}, "
              f"k {k:.2f}, b {b:.2f})", "L0", [str(OUT), str(kst.BIN), SCRIPT], notes=f"prereg {regs[0]['id']}")
"""Shear-curvature volume transfer (swarm S1, open front, Opus): a new observable for the champion's mechanism.

python scripts/k_shear_transfer.py
Claim: the clamped mixing shear curvatures of random fcc alloys are pair sums of 50:50 binary curvatures taken at the
alloy's own volume, K_alloy(V0) = sum 4 x_i x_j K_ij(V0), with no parameter. Baseline: the same pair sum at each
binary's own Vegard volume V_ij.
Order, so that the test is blind:
 1. binaries: K44, K' of the 50:50 binaries (SQS seeds 0-2) on a ln(V/V_ij) grid -> data/binary_kgrid.csv
 2. predictions on the h3_fresh compositions (comp_actual, n_el >= 3; K never computed there), power by simulation,
    pre-registration in the ledger
 3. targets: the same a2 protocol on those alloys, references at the cell's actual fractions -> data/h3_shear_clamped.csv
 4. test: per channel RMSE(rule) <= 0.9 RMSE(pair at V_ij) and paired sign-flip p < 0.005 (two channels); PASS needs
    both channels. Secondary (reported, not gated): Opus's prior on median dlnK/dlnV of binaries with |K| > 10 GPa,
    K44 in [-5, -1.5], K' in [-6, -2].
"""

import datetime as dt
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-omat-0"
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
from ase.build import bulk  # noqa: E402
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline  # noqa: E402

from harness import compute, ledger  # noqa: E402
from harness.compute import GPA  # noqa: E402
from harness.context import context  # noqa: E402
from harness.features import parse_comp  # noqa: E402

AMPS = np.array([-0.01, -0.005, 0.0, 0.005, 0.01])
GRID = [-0.40, -0.30, -0.20, -0.15, -0.10, -0.05, 0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40]
BIN, TGT = ROOT / "data" / "binary_kgrid.csv", ROOT / "data" / "h3_shear_clamped.csv"
ctx = context()
calc = compute.calculator()
SCRIPT = str(Path(__file__))


def e_strained(atoms, v_atom, F):
    a = atoms.copy()
    a.set_cell(a.cell * (v_atom * len(a) / a.get_volume()) ** (1 / 3), scale_atoms=True)
    a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True)
    a.calc = calc
    t = time.perf_counter()
    e = a.get_potential_energy() / len(a)
    time.sleep(time.perf_counter() - t)  # 50% duty cycle, keeps the laptop cool
    return e


def F_of(name, s):
    if name == "K44":
        F = np.eye(3)
        F[0, 1] = s
        return F
    return np.diag([np.exp(s), np.exp(-s), 1.0])


def curvatures(alloy, x, v):
    """K44, Kp (GPa) of E_mix with references at fractions x, all at volume v and the same deformation."""
    pures = {el: bulk(el, "fcc", a=4.0, cubic=True) for el in x}
    out = {}
    for name in ("K44", "Kp"):
        em = [e_strained(alloy, v, F_of(name, s)) - sum(xi * e_strained(pures[el], v, F_of(name, s))
                                                         for el, xi in x.items()) for s in AMPS]
        c2 = np.polyfit(AMPS, em, 2)[0]
        out[name] = (2 * c2 if name == "K44" else c2 / 2) / v * GPA
    return out


# 1. binaries
done = set(map(tuple, pd.read_csv(BIN)[["pair", "seed", "dlnV"]].astype(str).values)) if BIN.exists() else set()
for (A, B), p in sorted(ctx.pair.items()):
    for seed in (0, 1, 2):
        alloy = compute.solid_solution({A: 0.5, B: 0.5}, "fcc", reps=3, seed=seed)
        for d in GRID:
            if (f"{A}-{B}", str(seed), str(d)) in done:
                continue
            v = p["V"] * np.exp(d)
            r = {"pair": f"{A}-{B}", "seed": seed, "dlnV": d, "V": v, **curvatures(alloy, {A: 0.5, B: 0.5}, v)}
            pd.DataFrame([r]).to_csv(BIN, mode="a", header=not BIN.exists(), index=False)
    print("binary", A, B, flush=True)

g = pd.read_csv(BIN).groupby(["pair", "dlnV"])[["K44", "Kp"]].mean().reset_index()
spl = {(tuple(k.split("-")), ch): CubicSpline(s.dlnV, s[ch]) for k, s in g.groupby("pair") for ch in ("K44", "Kp")}

# 2. predictions, power, pre-registration
h3 = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "h3_fresh_rows_fixed.csv")
h3 = h3[h3.n_el >= 3].reset_index(drop=True)
comps = [parse_comp(s) for s in h3.comp_actual]
keep = [all(((a, b), "K44") in spl for a, b, _, _ in ctx.pairs(c)) for c in comps]
h3, comps = h3[keep].reset_index(drop=True), [c for c, k in zip(comps, keep) if k]


def predict(c, ch, at_alloy):
    v0 = ctx.vegard(c)
    return sum(4 * xa * xb * float(spl[((a, b), ch)](np.log(v0 / ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"]) if at_alloy else 0.0))
               for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))


P = {ch: (np.array([predict(c, ch, True) for c in comps]), np.array([predict(c, ch, False) for c in comps]))
     for ch in ("K44", "Kp")}


def test(y, rule, pair, n_perm=4000, seed=0):
    e_r, e_p = y - rule, y - pair
    gain = 1 - np.sqrt(np.mean(e_r**2)) / np.sqrt(np.mean(e_p**2))
    d = e_p**2 - e_r**2
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    null = np.array([(d * rng.choice([-1, 1], len(d))).mean() for _ in range(n_perm)])
    p = (np.sum(null >= d.mean()) + 1) / (n_perm + 1)
    return gain >= 0.10 and p < 0.005, float(gain), float(p)


# Realistic scatter = the rule's residual on the exploratory a2 rows (h1 compositions, n_el >= 3), the arena's
# convention. A first design used the pair sum's residual there (4 GPa, includes the transfer signal itself) and had
# power 0.45, so it was not registered and no target was computed (ledger design note).
a2 = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / "a2_shear_clamped.csv")
a2c = [parse_comp(s) for s in a2.comp]
a2k = [len(c) >= 3 and all(((a, b), "K44") in spl for a, b, _, _ in ctx.pairs(c)) for c in a2c]
a2, a2c = a2[a2k], [c for c, k in zip(a2c, a2k) if k]
SIG = {ch: float(np.sqrt(np.mean((a2[ch].values - [sum(4 * xa * xb * float(spl[((a, b), ch)](np.log(v / ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"])))
                                                        for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c)) for c, v in zip(a2c, a2.V0)])**2)))
       for ch in ("K44", "Kp")}
regs = [e for e in ledger.entries() if e["claim"].startswith("Shear-curvature volume transfer") and "prereg" in e["notes"]]
if not regs:
    if not any(e["claim"].startswith("Design note, shear-curvature transfer") for e in ledger.entries()):
        ledger.record("Design note, shear-curvature transfer: first design (sigma 4 GPa = pair-sum residual on exploratory "
                      "a2 rows) had power 0.45 and was not registered; no h3 target computed. Exploratory a2 (n 62, "
                      "seen): K44 pair 3.56 -> rule 2.66 GPa, Kp 5.67 -> 1.80, refit k 0.90 / 1.05. Redesign: sigma = "
                      f"rule residual on a2 {SIG}, the arena convention", "L0", [SCRIPT, str(BIN)],
                      notes="design; before registration")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    sim = lambda truth: np.mean([all(test(P[ch][truth] + rng.normal(0, SIG[ch], len(comps)),  # noqa: E731
                                          *P[ch], 1000, i)[0] for ch in P) for i in range(200)])
    power, fp = sim(0), sim(1)
    print(f"n {len(comps)}, power {power:.3f}, false pass {fp:.3f}", flush=True)
    reg = ledger.register(f"Shear-curvature volume transfer: clamped mixing K44 and K' of random fcc alloys equal "
                          f"sum 4 x_i x_j K_ij(V0) with binary curvatures at the alloy volume (no parameter); PASS if "
                          f"in both channels RMSE <= 0.9 x pair-at-V_ij and sign-flip p < 0.005 on {len(comps)} h3_fresh "
                          f"alloys whose K has never been computed", SCRIPT, {"power": power, "false_pass": fp},
                          notes="proposed by Opus in swarm S1 (open front), critiqued by Astra; binaries computed first")
    print("registered", reg["id"], flush=True)
    regs = [reg]

# 3. targets
done = set(pd.read_csv(TGT)["comp"]) if TGT.exists() else set()
for s, c in zip(h3.comp_actual, comps):
    if s in done:
        continue
    alloy = compute.solid_solution(c, "fcc", reps=3, seed=0)
    x = compute.actual_fractions(alloy)
    assert max(abs(x[e] - c[e]) for e in c) < 1e-3, (s, x)
    r = {"comp": s, "n_el": len(c), "V0": ctx.vegard(c), **curvatures(alloy, x, ctx.vegard(c)),
         "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
    pd.DataFrame([r]).to_csv(TGT, mode="a", header=not TGT.exists(), index=False)
print("targets done", flush=True)

# 4. test
t = pd.read_csv(TGT).set_index("comp").loc[h3.comp_actual]
res = {}
for ch in ("K44", "Kp"):
    y = t[ch].values
    ok, gain, p = test(y, *P[ch])
    rm = lambda e: float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(e))))  # noqa: E731
    T = P[ch][0] - P[ch][1]
    k = float(T @ (y - P[ch][1]) / (T @ T))
    res[ch] = ok
    print(f"{ch}: raw {rm(y - y.mean()):.2f}, pair at V_ij {rm(y - P[ch][1]):.2f}, rule {rm(y - P[ch][0]):.2f} GPa, "
          f"gain {gain:.2f}, p {p:.1e}, refit k {k:.2f} -> {'pass' if ok else 'fail'}", flush=True)
sl = {}
for ch in ("K44", "Kp"):
    vals = [float(spl[((tuple(k.split('-'))), ch)](0, 1) / spl[((tuple(k.split('-'))), ch)](0))
            for k in g.pair.unique() if abs(spl[((tuple(k.split('-'))), ch)](0)) > 10]
    sl[ch] = (len(vals), float(np.median(vals)) if vals else float("nan"))
print("secondary: median dlnK/dlnV of binaries with |K| > 10 GPa:", sl, flush=True)
passed = all(res.values())
if __name__ == "__main__":  # k_shear_kp_hm.py imports this file for its splines; the h3 result is recorded once
    ledger.record(f"Shear-curvature volume transfer: {'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'} on {len(comps)} unseen h3 alloys "
              f"(K44 {'pass' if res['K44'] else 'fail'}, Kp {'pass' if res['Kp'] else 'fail'}); binary slope prior {sl}",
              "L0", [str(BIN), str(TGT), SCRIPT], notes=f"prereg {regs[0]['id']}")

1: """Structure generation, relaxation and elastic constants with a universal ML potential."""
2: 
3: from __future__ import annotations
4: 
5: import datetime as dt
6: import os
7: import time
8: from functools import lru_cache
9: 
10: import numpy as np
11: from ase import Atoms
12: from ase.build import bulk
13: from ase.filters import FrechetCellFilter
14: from ase.optimize import FIRE
15: 
16: from harness.reference import ELASTIC_EXP
17: 
18: GPA = 160.21766208  # eV/A^3 -> GPa
19: MODEL = os.environ.get("HARNESS_MODEL", "medium-omat-0")  # mace_mp foundation model name
20: 
21: # Rough lattice parameters (A) for the starting guess only; relaxation sets the real value.
22: A0 = {"fcc": {"Al": 4.05, "Cu": 3.61, "Ni": 3.52, "Ag": 4.09, "Au": 4.08, "Pd": 3.89,
23:               "Pt": 3.92, "Co": 3.54, "Fe": 3.59, "Cr": 3.60, "Mn": 3.60},
24:       "bcc": {"Fe": 2.87, "Cr": 2.88, "Mo": 3.15, "W": 3.16, "V": 3.03, "Nb": 3.30,
25:               "Ta": 3.30, "Ti": 3.28, "Zr": 3.57, "Hf": 3.50, "Al": 3.24}}
26: 
27: 
28: @lru_cache(maxsize=1)
29: def calculator():
30:     from mace.calculators import mace_mp
31:     import torch
32:     device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
33:     return mace_mp(model=MODEL, device=device, default_dtype="float64")
34: 
35: 
36: def site_counts(comp: dict[str, float], n: int) -> dict[str, int]:
37:     counts = {el: int(round(x * n)) for el, x in comp.items()}
38:     counts[max(counts, key=counts.get)] += n - sum(counts.values())
39:     return counts
40: 
41: 
42: def actual_fractions(atoms: Atoms) -> dict[str, float]:
43:     """Composition the cell really has. Subtract pure references with these, not the nominal fractions (the
44:     rounding to whole atoms shifted E_mix by up to ~57 meV/atom before 2026-10-31)."""
45:     s = atoms.get_chemical_symbols()
46:     return {el: s.count(el) / len(s) for el in sorted(set(s))}
47: 
48: 
49: def solid_solution(comp: dict[str, float], lattice: str, reps: int, seed: int) -> Atoms:
50:     """Random solid solution on a cubic conventional supercell (no SQS optimisation). Counts are rounded to whole
51:     atoms; use actual_fractions() for references."""
52:     a = sum(x * A0[lattice].get(el, 3.5 if lattice == "fcc" else 3.1) for el, x in comp.items())
53:     atoms = bulk("X", lattice, a=a, cubic=True).repeat((reps, reps, reps))
54:     counts = site_counts(comp, len(atoms))
55:     symbols = [el for el, c in counts.items() for _ in range(c)]
56:     np.random.default_rng(seed).shuffle(symbols)
57:     atoms.set_chemical_symbols(symbols)
58:     return atoms
59: 
60: 
61: # GPU duty cycle in (0, 1]: after each relaxation sleep so the GPU is busy only this fraction
62: # of the time. Keeps a laptop from overheating on long scans; results are unaffected.
63: DUTY = float(os.environ.get("HARNESS_DUTY", "1.0"))
64: 
65: 
66: def relax(atoms: Atoms, cell: bool, fmax: float = 1e-3, steps: int = 400) -> int:
67:     atoms.calc = calculator()
68:     target = FrechetCellFilter(atoms) if cell else atoms
69:     opt = FIRE(target, logfile=None)
70:     t = time.perf_counter()
71:     opt.run(fmax=fmax, steps=steps)
72:     if DUTY < 1:
73:         time.sleep((time.perf_counter() - t) * (1 / DUTY - 1))
74:     return opt.nsteps
75: 
76: 
77: def elastic_tensor(atoms: Atoms, eps: float = 0.005, relax_ions: bool = True) -> np.ndarray:
78:     """Full 6x6 Voigt tensor (GPa) from central differences of stress, ions relaxed at each strain."""
79:     cell0 = atoms.get_cell().array.copy()
80:     C = np.zeros((6, 6))
81:     voigt = [(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 2), (0, 2), (0, 1)]
82:     for j, (k, l) in enumerate(voigt):
83:         sig = []
84:         for s in (+eps, -eps):
85:             e = np.zeros((3, 3))
86:             if k == l:
87:                 e[k, k] = s
88:             else:
89:                 e[k, l] = e[l, k] = s / 2  # engineering shear strain = s
90:             strained = atoms.copy()
91:             strained.set_cell(cell0 @ (np.eye(3) + e), scale_atoms=True)
92:             strained.calc = calculator()
93:             if relax_ions and len(strained) > 1:
94:                 relax(strained, cell=False, fmax=5e-4)
95:             sig.append(strained.get_stress(voigt=True) * GPA)  # ASE: tensile stress positive
96:         C[:, j] = (sig[0] - sig[1]) / (2 * eps)
97:     return 0.5 * (C + C.T)
98: 
99: 
100: def cubic_average(C: np.ndarray) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
101:     """Project a (noisy, random alloy) 6x6 tensor onto cubic symmetry."""
102:     c11 = np.mean([C[0, 0], C[1, 1], C[2, 2]])
103:     c12 = np.mean([C[0, 1], C[0, 2], C[1, 2]])
104:     c44 = np.mean([C[3, 3], C[4, 4], C[5, 5]])
105:     return float(c11), float(c12), float(c44)
106: 
107: 
108: def voigt_reuss_hill(c11: float, c12: float, c44: float) -> dict[str, float]:
109:     B = (c11 + 2 * c12) / 3
110:     Gv = (c11 - c12 + 3 * c44) / 5
111:     Gr = 5 * (c11 - c12) * c44 / (4 * c44 + 3 * (c11 - c12))
112:     G = (Gv + Gr) / 2
113:     E = 9 * B * G / (3 * B + G)
114:     nu = (3 * B - 2 * G) / (2 * (3 * B + G))
115:     return {"B": B, "G": G, "E": E, "nu": nu, "pugh": B / G, "cauchy": c12 - c44,
116:             "zener": 2 * c44 / (c11 - c12)}
117: 
118: 
119: def run_alloy(comp: dict[str, float], lattice: str, reps: int = 3, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
120:     atoms = solid_solution(comp, lattice, reps, seed)
121:     nsteps = relax(atoms, cell=True)
122:     C = elastic_tensor(atoms)
123:     c11, c12, c44 = cubic_average(C)
124:     # Quality flag: spread of the three cubic-equivalent C11 and C44 entries. Large spread means the
125:     # random cell is too small for its chemistry or the solid solution broke symmetry on relaxing.
126:     spread = float(max(np.ptp(np.diag(C)[:3]) / c11, np.ptp(np.diag(C)[3:]) / max(c44, 1.0)))
127:     vol = atoms.get_volume() / len(atoms)
128:     row = {"formula": atoms.get_chemical_formula(mode="metal"),
129:            "comp": ";".join(f"{el}:{x:.4f}" for el, x in sorted(comp.items())),
130:            "lattice": lattice, "natoms": len(atoms), "seed": seed, "model": MODEL,
131:            "vol_per_atom": vol, "a_eff": (vol * (4 if lattice == "fcc" else 2)) ** (1 / 3),
132:            "relax_steps": nsteps, "cubic_spread": spread, "C11": c11, "C12": c12, "C44": c44,
133:            "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
134:     row.update(voigt_reuss_hill(c11, c12, c44))
135:     return row
136: 
137: 
138: def calibrate(elements: list[str] | None = None) -> list[dict]:
139:     rows = []
140:     for el in elements or list(ELASTIC_EXP):
141:         lattice, e11, e12, e44 = ELASTIC_EXP[el]
142:         r = run_alloy({el: 1.0}, lattice, reps=1)
143:         r["el"] = el
144:         r.update({"C11_exp": e11, "C12_exp": e12, "C44_exp": e44})
145:         r.update({f"{k}_exp": v for k, v in voigt_reuss_hill(e11, e12, e44).items()})
146:         rows.append(r)
147:     return rows

23:     if not LEDGER.exists():
24:         return []
25:     return [json.loads(line) for line in LEDGER.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line]
26: 
27: 
28: def record(claim: str, level: str, evidence: list[str], notes: str = "",
29:            parent: str | None = None) -> dict:
30:     assert level in LEVELS, level
31:     if level in ("L2", "L3", "L4"):
32:         below = LEVELS[LEVELS.index(level) - 1]
33:         known = {e.get("id"): e["level"] for e in entries()}
34:         if known.get(parent) != below:
35:             raise ValueError(f"{level} claim needs a parent entry at {below}, got {parent!r}")
36:     now = dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
37:     entry = {"id": hashlib.sha256(f"{now}{claim}".encode()).hexdigest()[:10], "time": now,
38:              "level": level, "claim": claim, "parent": parent,
39:              "evidence": {str(p): file_hash(p) for p in evidence}, "notes": notes}
40:     LEDGER.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
41:     with LEDGER.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
42:         f.write(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
43:     return entry
44: 
45: 
46: # Pre-registration and verdicts. A test is registered with its measured power (harness/power.py): a design in which
47: # a correct formula usually fails is not a test. A failed test is closed with a cause; only cause "hypothesis" retires
48: # the candidate, "design" and "numerics" send it back to the queue.
49: CAUSES = ("pass", "hypothesis", "design", "numerics")
50: 
51: 
52: def register(claim: str, script: str, power: dict, notes: str = "") -> dict:
53:     if power.get("power", 0) < 0.8 or power.get("false_pass", 1) > 0.05:
54:         raise ValueError(f"underpowered or leaky test design, not registered: {power}")
55:     return record(claim, "L0", [script], notes=f"prereg; power {power}; {notes}".strip("; "))
56: 
57: 
58: def verdict(prereg: str, outcome: str, cause: str, audit: str, evidence: list[str]) -> dict:
59:     assert cause in CAUSES, cause
60:     if cause == "hypothesis" and not audit.strip():
61:         raise ValueError("retiring a candidate needs a post-fail audit (what was checked, by whom)")
62:     return record(f"verdict on {prereg}: {outcome}", "L0", evidence, notes=f"cause={cause}; audit: {audit}")
63: 
64: 
65: def open_candidates() -> list[dict]:
66:     """Registered candidates without a verdict, or whose last verdict was a design or numerics failure."""
67:     es = entries()
68:     last = {}
69:     for e in es:
70:         if e["claim"].startswith("verdict on "):
71:             last[e["claim"].split()[2].rstrip(":")] = e["notes"]
72:     return [e for e in es if e["notes"].startswith("prereg")
73:             and ("cause=pass" not in last.get(e["id"], "") and "cause=hypothesis" not in last.get(e["id"], ""))]
FILE .orchestra/LESSONS.md
1: # Lessons for derivation agents (Astra, Opus)
2: 
3: Read before proposing. Each line is a way a candidate died or nearly died for the wrong reason. Updated 2026-10-31.
4: 
5: 1. Ratios of energies blow up where the denominator crosses zero (R3: n_eff = -3 b/a reached -102 for Cu-Ir). Prefer
6:    predictions linear in measured quantities; if a ratio is essential, say where it is undefined.
7: 2. Compare like with like: clamped with clamped, relaxed with relaxed, random with random. R3 compared a relaxed random
8:    volume with a clamped L1_0 volume; even the exact formula then had slope 0.20.
9: 3. Ordered cells are not random alloys. In PBE, 4-atom ordered cells carry a fixed-volume many-body term (~10 meV/atom)
10:    that random alloys lack. A random-alloy rule must be tested on random (SQS) cells.
11: 4. If your rule's main content is a common shift, a test with a free intercept cannot see it. State the test you expect
12:    to pass, and check its power by simulation (harness/power.py) before data exist.
13: 5. Results that survived so far: volume transfer of binary interactions (L2, refit k = 0.79 on both holdouts, not
14:    input noise); isotropic chemical shear softening K44 ~ K' in Ir/Rh alloys (MACE, PBE pending). Build on these.
15: 6. Results that died for real: A2 (shear from hydrostatic derivatives; even a free 2-term fit has r 0.37), H-sm
16:    (predicted K44/K' = 4, measured 1.05), R3b (exponent sharing). Do not resubmit without a new mechanism.
17: 7. PBE: pure references must share the alloy's cutoff (dft.Settings(ecut_elements=...)). Earlier PBE mixing numbers
18:    carry a cutoff mismatch; its size is being measured (data/ecut_bias.csv).
19: 8. Round R1 (Astra and Opus independently): 108-atom cells round atom counts, but references used nominal fractions,
20:    so every non-integer composition carried up to ~60 meV/atom of bookkeeping error. Fixed in data/*_fixed.csv
21:    (column comp_actual is the real composition) and in the generators. Always reference the composition the cell has.
22: 9. PBE cutoff mismatch corrected (harness/ecutfix.py, validated to 0.002 meV/atom). MACE now PASSES L1 for the
23:    ordered-cell beyond-pair Delta (sign 9/10, r 0.80); PBE quaternary Delta +12.9 meV is real. MACE data on ordered
24:    multicomponent cells can be used.
25: 10. Round R2 (Astra): the arena's permutation count capped the smallest reachable p at 1/501, so after five tests no
26:     candidate could pass however good it was. Fixed: n_perm grows with m. Also open: generators set V0 from nominal
27:     fractions while comp_actual differs (~0.5% in volume, ~0.06 meV RMSE effect, not the cause of k ~ 0.8).
28: 11. k ~ 0.8 was mostly linearisation: E_ij(V) is strongly nonlinear over |ln(V0/V_ij)| up to 0.36. Exact binary
29:     energies at the alloy volume give k 0.94 [0.90, 0.98] and RMSE 10.3 meV with no parameter (data/binary_vgrid.csv).
30: 12. Swarm S1 audit (Astra): (a) scripts/hiso_l12.py did not use ecut_elements, and harness/dft.py picks the k-grid
31:     from the strained cell (18x18x18 vs 17x18x18), so 0.1 meV/atom of strain-dependent error moves K by 1.6 to 4.7
32:     GPa. H-iso results before the fix are not evidence either way; the run is stopped. (b) fix_counts.py treated
33:     0.3333 as the reference weight of equiatomic ternaries (36+36+36 atoms are exact): +0.3 to +0.7 meV added.
34:     (c) B_chem and R in *_fixed.csv are stale. (d) K44 ~ K' is not Zener invariance.
35: 13. k at fixed composition (h1/h3 E(V) curves vs exact binary response): 0.976 [0.956, 1.001]. No reduced volume
36:     response; k ~ 0.8 is the curvature the linear transfer leaves out (94% of the shift).
37: 
38: 14. Shear-curvature volume transfer (prereg 4c29d9754c, result 6e0923b413), 113 unseen h3 alloys, binary curvatures
39:     at the alloy volume, no parameter. Kp: 4.77 -> 2.03 GPa, gain 0.57, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08 (pass). K44: 3.29 -> 2.62,
40:     gain 0.20, p 0.023, refit k 0.86 (fail at p < 0.005). Joint claim FAIL. The first design (sigma = pair-sum residual,
41:     which contains the signal) had power 0.45 and was stopped before any target existed. K44's worst rule errors are
42:     Co-rich (Co ~0.46 with Pt or Cu), where the rule is worse than no transfer; cause not yet audited (hypothesis,
43:     design or numerics). Do not re-split the joint claim after the fact: a K44 or Kp claim needs its own fresh test.
44: 
45: 15. K' alone, fresh blind test (prereg 67a358fc59, result d92844787f, L2 entry recorded): 94 hm_fresh alloys, K' 4.22 ->
46:     1.89 GPa, gain 0.55, p 2.5e-4, refit k 1.08, 75/94 better. Two independent blind sets now agree for K' (k 1.08 both).
47:     K44 again weaker (gain 0.12, k 0.69, not gated). Why K44 transfers worse than K' is open: Co-rich outliers, or
48:     internal (non-affine) relaxation channels that the clamped protocol suppresses differently for the two shears.
49: 
50: 16. Model swap of the K' rule (prereg 851aec6883, result 86767e478d): medium-mpa-0, same geometry, same 94 hm_fresh
51:     alloys, binaries seed 0 only. K' 4.73 -> 2.28 GPa, gain 0.52, p 2.5e-4, but refit k 1.33 [1.11, 1.51]: the
52:     pre-registered k-contains-1 condition FAILS. K44 gain 0.16, k 0.77. Reading: that the alloy's K' follows the binaries
53:     at the alloy volume and cuts the error in half survives a model with a different shear bias; that the coefficient is
54:     exactly 1 does not (omat 1.08 twice, mpa 1.33). Binary seed noise would pull k down, not up. The two models disagree
55:     most at |dlnV| > 0.2 (K' corr 0.80 vs 0.96 within 0.1). Cause not yet audited. Do not claim "parameter-free" across
56:     models; the PBE check decides which k is physical.
57: 
58: 17. K44 transfer fails only with Co (prereg e410c96a32, result d9460850ce). 120 fresh Co-free alloys: K44 pair 4.68 ->
59:     rule 2.30 GPa, gain 0.51, p 2.5e-4, k 1.23 (PASS). 60 fresh alloys with Co >= 15%: gain 0.11, p 0.08, k 0.70. K'
60:     passes in both. Open confound: the Co-free set has a larger volume signal (pair error 4.68 vs 3.36), so "Co breaks
61:     K44" and "K44 needs a large signal" are not yet separated; match the two sets on |rule - pair| before claiming
62:     a Co mechanism (magnetism is a guess, MACE has no spin).
63:     Confound check (exploratory, same fresh rows, tertiles of |rule - pair|): at matched signal Co-free gain 0.37 / 0.58
64:     vs Co 0.08 / 0.22 (mid / large), and Co alloys carry a larger floor at small signal (rule rms 2.61 vs 1.73 GPa).
65:     The Co effect survives signal matching; not yet a registered claim.
66: 
67: 18. Why K44 looked broken (Opus, swarm S2, blind by file timestamp, confirmed on 60 Co alloys). The part the pair rule
68:     misses is the same in both shears (corr 0.71, slope ~1). K44's volume signal is half of K''s, so the shared floor
69:     swamps it; in Co alloys the floor anticorrelates with the signal and drags k to 0.7. Remove the floor (A = K44 - K'
70:     or e' as covariate) and K44 transfers with k ~1. LESSONS 14-16 failure reason: design, not hypothesis.
71: 
72: 19. Shared SQS seed leak (Opus S2 audit, Astra confirmed). compute.py:56 draws the site permutation from (seed, n)
73:     only, so every seed-0 cell thresholds one random field: seed-0 targets and seed-0 binaries share configuration
74:     noise. K' is immune (gain 0.55-0.58, k 1.07-1.10 for every seed split). K44 is not: leak-free gain 0.06-0.14,
75:     k 0.60-0.77. d9460850ce and the LESSONS 18 Co check used the leak; 9cfc8edaf0 was withdrawn before reading and
76:     re-registered as c2eff007ad with target seed 100. Rule: targets and inputs never share a seed.

.orchestra/swarm/S2/audit\opus.md:3:Three findings. The largest is a harness error: every 108-atom cell built with the same seed uses the same random site permutation. So seed-0 alloy targets and seed-0 binary inputs share their configurational noise. That inflates the K44 transfer and could flip a pre-registered verdict. The K' L2 result and the energy champion survive it.

.orchestra/swarm/S2/k44\opus.md:1:K44 is no less pair-additive than K'. What the rule misses is the same number of GPa in both channels, so the anisotropy K44 − K' transfers cleanly. K44 fails the test for two design reasons: its volume signal is half of K''s, and in Co alloys the shared residual happens to anticorrelate with that signal. The audit reason for LESSONS 14 to 16 should be `design`, not `hypothesis`.
.orchestra/swarm/S2/k44\opus.md:6:1. **The rule's error is shared between channels.** The K44 rule residual equals the K' residual: slope 1.04, r 0.77 on 269 omat rows, and slope 1.14, r 0.65 under mpa. The two channels' single-cell (seed) noise does not explain this: seed deviations correlate at −0.22.
.orchestra/swarm/S2/k44\opus.md:12:1. **Residual stress picked up by simple shear.** The cells' deviatoric σ_yy is only 0.15 to 0.27 GPa rms. It anticorrelates with the K44 seed deviation (r −0.54), and subtracting it makes the seed scatter worse.

.orchestra/swarm/S2/k44\critique_of_astra_by_opus.md:1:{"item": "astra_1", "verdict": "DROP", "prior": "KNOWN", "refs": ["Redlich & Kister 1948, Ind. Eng. Chem. 40:345, [doi:10.1021/ie50458a036](https://doi.org/10.1021/ie50458a036): the antisymmetric first term x(1-x)(1-2x)", "Wang et al. 2016, CALPHAD-type modelling of single-crystal elastic constants in Ti-Nb-Zr, [PMID 27235781](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27235781/)", "Lin, Shang, ..., Liu 2024, CALPHAD modelling of shear properties of Ni alloys, [2404.19098](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19098)"], "why": "The citations and numbers check out. a2 lines 57 and 69 are Co0.75Ir0.25 and Co0.25Pt0.75, with r44/rp of -7.66/-6.33 and +4.44/+3.60 against the 3-seed binary_kgrid splines. All three fixed predictions reproduce exactly from 1.5*K50(V) - K(complement). But r(1-x) = -r(x) is the subregular first Redlich-Kister term, a known form. It also does not answer the front. (a) It does not single out one channel: the same rows carry nearly equal K44 and Kp residuals, and Kp still transfers with gain 0.55. (b) It is not specific to Co. The largest 25/75 binary residuals include Cu-Rh +6.7/+7.6, Cu-Ir -5.7, Au-Ir -5.2 and Au-Rh -4.6, while the K44 residual is under 1 GPa for Co-Ni, Co-Cu, Ag-Co and Au-Co. (c) Each fixed prediction inherits the seed-0 error of the old row. K44 seed SD at V_ij is 2.1 to 2.4 GPa for Co-Ir, Co-Pt and Cu-Pt (seed-0 Cu-Pt 50:50 alone sits -2.4 from the mean), the tolerances are 2.5 to 3, and no power was computed, so a true hypothesis would often fail. (d) The L1 term vanishes for any pair with x_i = x_j, so in multicomponent alloys it only matters for strongly off-equiatomic pairs. It could come back as a subregular extension of the rule covering both channels, but not as the explanation for K44."}
.orchestra/swarm/S2/k44\critique_of_astra_by_opus.md:2:{"item": "astra_2", "verdict": "KEEP", "prior": "KNOWN", "refs": ["Tasnadi, Oden, Abrikosov 2012, PRB 85:144112, elastic constants vs supercell size and shape, cubic projection, [1111.0548](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.0548)", "Tian et al. 2015, JPCM 27:315702, uncertainty from symmetry lowering in SQS elastic constants exceeds the SQS vs CPA difference, [PMID 26202339](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26202339/)", "Moakher & Norris 2006, J. Elasticity 85:215, closest cubic tensor", "Caro 2014, projection onto higher symmetry, [1408.1219](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.1219)"], "why": "The file citations are correct. compute.py:49-58 shuffles without SQS, k_shear_transfer.py:56-60 uses only xy simple shear, and line 156 computes targets at seed 0. Seed SD at V_ij for the 4 pairs reproduces (K44 1.93, Kp 0.45). The 'whole grid' figures 1.93/1.17 are actually the all-36-pair values; the 4 named pairs over the grid give 2.67/1.25. I checked the physics with 108 MACE single points (36 pairs x 3 seeds). Deviatoric stress in the clamped cells is only 0.17 GPa RMS, so the sigma_yy term that simple shear adds through E_yy = g^2/2 is not the source. The K44 scatter follows cell anisotropy instead (dK44 vs dsigma_yy r = -0.54), and averaging over shear planes removes exactly that. Extra issue found: for a given seed and cell size, rng.shuffle applies the same permutation, so every seed-0 50:50 binary has identical sites and multicomponent seed-0 cells are nested in them (verified). Seed-0 K44 averages 0.50 GPa below the 3-seed mean over all 36 pairs. All h3, hm and cofree targets use seed 0, so their noise is correlated across rows, which the sign-flip test assumes away. Limits: the method is textbook, not a physics claim. If multicomponent targets carry binary-level noise of 1.4 to 1.9 GPa, removing it lifts the h3 K44 gain from 0.20 to about 0.3 at most, still below Kp's 0.55. Co pairs do not have larger seed SD than non-Co pairs (Cu-Ir 2.9, Ni-Pt 2.5, Ag-Ir 2.5), so this cannot explain the Co split in LESSONS 17. Keep it as a design/numerics fix to run before any new K44 test, with fresh seeds. At about 1 s per 108-atom single point on this machine, it costs roughly 1 to 2 hours, not 5 to 30 CPU-hours."}

17. K44 transfer fails only with Co (prereg e410c96a32, result d9460850ce). 120 fresh Co-free alloys: K44 pair 4.68 ->
    rule 2.30 GPa, gain 0.51, p 2.5e-4, k 1.23 (PASS). 60 fresh alloys with Co >= 15%: gain 0.11, p 0.08, k 0.70. K'
    passes in both. Open confound: the Co-free set has a larger volume signal (pair error 4.68 vs 3.36), so "Co breaks
    K44" and "K44 needs a large signal" are not yet separated; match the two sets on |rule - pair| before claiming
    a Co mechanism (magnetism is a guess, MACE has no spin).
    Confound check (exploratory, same fresh rows, tertiles of |rule - pair|): at matched signal Co-free gain 0.37 / 0.58
    vs Co 0.08 / 0.22 (mid / large), and Co alloys carry a larger floor at small signal (rule rms 2.61 vs 1.73 GPa).
    The Co effect survives signal matching; not yet a registered claim.

18. Why K44 looked broken (Opus, swarm S2, blind by file timestamp, confirmed on 60 Co alloys). The part the pair rule
    misses is the same in both shears (corr 0.71, slope ~1). K44's volume signal is half of K''s, so the shared floor
    swamps it; in Co alloys the floor anticorrelates with the signal and drags k to 0.7. Remove the floor (A = K44 - K'
    or e' as covariate) and K44 transfers with k ~1. LESSONS 14-16 failure reason: design, not hypothesis.

19. Shared SQS seed leak (Opus S2 audit, Astra confirmed). compute.py:56 draws the site permutation from (seed, n)
    only, so every seed-0 cell thresholds one random field: seed-0 targets and seed-0 binaries share configuration
    noise. K' is immune (gain 0.55-0.58, k 1.07-1.10 for every seed split). K44 is not: leak-free gain 0.06-0.14,
    k 0.60-0.77. d9460850ce and the LESSONS 18 Co check used the leak; 9cfc8edaf0 was withdrawn before reading and
    re-registered as c2eff007ad with target seed 100. Rule: targets and inputs never share a seed.

1: """Fresh test of the shared-floor picture of shear transfer (LESSONS 18; Opus, swarm S2 k44 front).
2: 
3: python scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py
4: Seen so far (k44_cofree Co set, blind by file timestamp only): the residual of the volume-transfer pair rule is the
5: same in both shears, so the anisotropy A = K44 - K' transfers as sum 4 x_i x_j A_ij(V0) and K44 transfers with k ~1
6: once e' = K' - rule' is a covariate. Here both are pre-registered in the ledger on 150 new random alloys (half with
7: Co >= 15%), drawn with a new seed and never computed. Targets use SQS seed 100: binaries use seeds 0-2, and compute.py:56
8: makes the site permutation depend only on (seed, n), so a shared seed leaks configuration noise (S2 audit, ledger
9: withdrawal of 9cfc8edaf0). Plain K44 per Co set is reported, not gated.
10: PASS needs all three: (1) A rule: RMSE <= 0.9 x pair-at-V_ij and sign-flip p < 0.005; (2) corr(e44, e') >= 0.5;
11: (3) joint fit K44 - pair44 = k T44 + b e': k and b both in [0.7, 1.3].
12: """
13: 
14: import datetime as dt
15: import sys
16: from pathlib import Path
17: 
18: ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
19: sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
20: import importlib.util  # noqa: E402
21: 
22: import numpy as np  # noqa: E402
23: import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402
24: 
25: from harness import ledger  # noqa: E402
26: 
27: spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("kst", ROOT / "scripts" / "k_shear_transfer.py")
28: kst = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
29: spec.loader.exec_module(kst)
30: from harness import compute  # noqa: E402
31: from harness.features import parse_comp  # noqa: E402
32: 
33: ctx, curvatures, test = kst.ctx, kst.curvatures, kst.test
34: g = kst.g.copy()
35: g["A"] = g.K44 - g.Kp
36: spl = {(tuple(k.split("-")), ch): kst.CubicSpline(s.dlnV, s[ch]) for k, s in g.groupby("pair") for ch in ("K44", "Kp", "A")}
37: OUT = ROOT / "data" / "k_aniso_s100_clamped.csv"
38: SCRIPT = str(Path(__file__))
39: CLAIM = "Shared shear floor, disjoint seeds"
40: ELS = ["Ag", "Au", "Co", "Cu", "Ir", "Ni", "Pd", "Pt", "Rh"]
41: N = 108
42: 
43: seen = set()
44: for f in ("a2_shear_clamped", "h3_shear_clamped", "hm_shear_clamped", "k44_cofree_clamped"):
45:     seen |= set(pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / f"{f}.csv").comp)
46: for f in ("h3_fresh_rows_fixed", "hm_fresh_rows_fixed"):
47:     seen |= set(pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / f"{f}.csv").comp_actual)
48: 
49: 
50: def draw(rng, with_co):
51:     while True:
52:         k = int(rng.integers(3, 6))
53:         pool = [e for e in ELS if e != "Co"]
54:         els = sorted(([*rng.choice(pool, k - 1, replace=False), "Co"]) if with_co else rng.choice(pool, k, replace=False))
55:         cnt = 11 + rng.multinomial(N - 11 * k, rng.dirichlet(np.ones(k)))
56:         c = {e: n / N for e, n in zip(els, cnt)}
57:         s = ";".join(f"{e}:{c[e]:.4f}" for e in sorted(c))
58:         if (not with_co or c["Co"] >= 0.15) and s not in seen:
59:             seen.add(s)
60:             return s, c
61: 
62: 
63: rng = np.random.default_rng(20261102)
64: comps = [draw(rng, i % 2 == 1) for i in range(150)]
65: 
66: 
67: def pr(c, ch, at):
68:     v = ctx.vegard(c)
69:     return sum(4 * xa * xb * float(spl[((a, b), ch)](np.log(v / ctx.pair[(a, b)]["V"]) if at else 0.0))
70:                for a, b, xa, xb in ctx.pairs(c))
71: 
72: 
73: P = {ch: (np.array([pr(c, ch, 1) for _, c in comps]), np.array([pr(c, ch, 0) for _, c in comps])) for ch in ("K44", "Kp", "A")}
74: 
75: 
76: def judge(y44, yp):
77:     okA, gain, p = test(y44 - yp, *P["A"])
78:     e44, ep = y44 - P["K44"][0], yp - P["Kp"][0]
79:     r = float(np.corrcoef(e44, ep)[0, 1])
80:     k, b = np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[P["K44"][0] - P["K44"][1], ep], y44 - P["K44"][1], rcond=None)[0]
81:     return okA and r >= 0.5 and 0.7 <= k <= 1.3 and 0.7 <= b <= 1.3, gain, p, r, float(k), float(b)
82: 
83: 
84: # realistic noise, from the rows already computed (seen): K' residual of the rule, and the A residual on top of it
85: seenrows = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data" / f"{f}.csv") for f in ("h3_shear_clamped", "hm_shear_clamped", "k44_cofree_clamped")])
86: sc = [parse_comp(s) for s in seenrows.comp]
87: ep_s = seenrows.Kp.values - np.array([pr(c, "Kp", 1) for c in sc])
88: eA_s = (seenrows.K44 - seenrows.Kp).values - np.array([pr(c, "A", 1) for c in sc])
89: SP, SA = 1.2 * float(np.std(ep_s)), 1.2 * float(np.std(eA_s))  # x1.2: seen rows carry the seed leak
90: regs = [e for e in ledger.entries() if e["claim"].startswith(CLAIM) and "prereg" in e["notes"]]
91: if not regs:
92:     r2 = np.random.default_rng(4)
93: 
94:     def sim(truth):
95:         hits = []
96:         for i in range(300):
97:             ep = r2.normal(0, SP, len(comps))
98:             yp = P["Kp"][0] + ep
99:             y44 = (P["K44"][0] if truth == 0 else P["K44"][1]) + ep + r2.normal(0, SA, len(comps))
100:             if truth == 1:
101:                 yp = P["Kp"][1] + ep
102:             hits.append(judge(y44, yp)[0])
103:         return float(np.mean(hits))
104: 
105:     power, fp = sim(0), sim(1)
106:     print(f"n {len(comps)}, sigma K' {SP:.2f}, sigma A {SA:.2f}, power {power:.3f}, false pass {fp:.3f}", flush=True)
107:     reg = ledger.register(f"{CLAIM}: in clamped random fcc alloys the volume-transfer pair rule misses a part common to "
108:                           f"K44 and K'; PASS if on {len(comps)} new random alloys (half Co >= 15%) (1) A = K44 - K' rule "
109:                           f"sum 4 x_i x_j A_ij(V0) has RMSE <= 0.9 x pair-at-V_ij and sign-flip p < 0.005, (2) "
110:                           f"corr(e44, e') >= 0.5, (3) joint fit K44 - pair44 = k T44 + b e' gives k, b in [0.7, 1.3]",
111:                           SCRIPT, {"power": power, "false_pass": fp},
112:                           notes="Opus swarm S2 k44 front; seen confirmation on k44_cofree Co set (LESSONS 18)")
113:     print("registered", reg["id"], flush=True)
114:     regs = [reg]
115: 
116: done = set(pd.read_csv(OUT)["comp"]) if OUT.exists() else set()
117: for s, c in comps:
118:     if s in done:
119:         continue
120:     alloy = compute.solid_solution(c, "fcc", reps=3, seed=100)
121:     x = compute.actual_fractions(alloy)
122:     r = {"comp": s, "n_el": len(c), "co": c.get("Co", 0.0), "V0": ctx.vegard(c), **curvatures(alloy, x, ctx.vegard(c)),
123:          "time": dt.datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")}
124:     pd.DataFrame([r]).to_csv(OUT, mode="a", header=not OUT.exists(), index=False)
125: print("aniso targets done", flush=True)
126: 
127: t = pd.read_csv(OUT).set_index("comp").loc[[s for s, _ in comps]]
128: ok, gain, p, r, k, b = judge(t.K44.values, t.Kp.values)
129: print(f"A rule gain {gain:.2f}, p {p:.1e}; corr(e44, e') {r:.2f}; joint k {k:.2f}, b {b:.2f} -> {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}",
130:       flush=True)
131: for lab, m in (("Co-free", t.co.values == 0), ("Co", t.co.values > 0)):
132:     T, Y = (P["K44"][0] - P["K44"][1])[m], (t.K44.values - P["K44"][1])[m]
133:     _, gn, pp = test(t.K44.values[m], P["K44"][0][m], P["K44"][1][m])
134:     print(f"not gated, plain K44 {lab} (n {m.sum()}): gain {gn:.2f}, p {pp:.1e}, k {T @ Y / (T @ T):.2f}", flush=True)
135: ledger.record(f"{CLAIM}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'} on {len(comps)} new alloys (A gain {gain:.2f}, p {p:.1e}, corr {r:.2f}, "
136:               f"k {k:.2f}, b {b:.2f})", "L0", [str(OUT), str(kst.BIN), SCRIPT], notes=f"prereg {regs[0]['id']}")

os.environ['MKL_NUM_THREADS']='1'

from types import SimpleNamespace
import numpy as np,pandas as pd
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline
ROOT=Path.cwd()
def parse_comp(s): return {k:float(v) for k,v in (t.split(':') for t in s.split(';'))}
def loadfunc(file,names):
    tree=ast.parse(Path(file).read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef) and n.name in names],type_ignores=[]),file,'exec'),globals())
pure=pd.read_csv('data/scan_fcc_omat_pure.csv').set_index('el').vol_per_atom.to_dict()
els=['Ag','Au','Co','Cu','Ir','Ni','Pd','Pt','Rh']
ctx=SimpleNamespace(vegard=lambda c:sum(x*pure[e] for e,x in c.items()),
    pair={p:{'V':(pure[p[0]]+pure[p[1]])/2} for p in combinations(els,2)},
    pairs=lambda c:((a,b,c[a],c[b]) for a,b in combinations(sorted(c),2)))
g=pd.read_csv('data/binary_kgrid.csv').groupby(['pair','dlnV'])[['K44','Kp']].mean().reset_index()

for f in ('a2_shear_clamped','h3_shear_clamped','hm_shear_clamped','k44_cofree_clamped'):

N=108; ELS=els
loadfunc('scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py',{'draw','pr','judge'})
loadfunc('scripts/k_shear_transfer.py',{'test'})
rng=np.random.default_rng(20261102)
comps=[draw(rng,i%2==1) for i in range(150)]
P={ch:(np.array([pr(c,ch,1) for _,c in comps]),np.array([pr(c,ch,0) for _,c in comps])) for ch in ('K44','Kp','A')}
t=pd.read_csv('data/k_aniso_s100_clamped.csv')
print('MATCH_DRAW',list(t.comp)==[s for s,c in comps], 'N/DUP',len(t),t.comp.duplicated().sum(),'TIME',t.time.min(),t.time.max())
y44,yp=t.K44.values,t.Kp.values
print('ORIGINAL_JUDGE',judge(y44,yp))
rm=lambda e:np.sqrt(np.mean(e**2))
for ch,y in [('K44',y44),('Kp',yp),('A',y44-yp)]:
    print('RMSE',ch,'pair',rm(y-P[ch][1]),'rule',rm(y-P[ch][0]))
e44=y44-P['K44'][0]; ep=yp-P['Kp'][0]; eA=e44-ep
T=P['K44'][0]-P['K44'][1]

print('ALGEBRA 1+ projection(eA)',1+np.linalg.lstsq(X,eA,rcond=None)[0], 'A_spline_identity',np.max(np.abs(P['A'][0]-(P['K44'][0]-P['Kp'][0]))))
rng=np.random.default_rng(111)
boot=[]
for _ in range(5000):
    ix=rng.integers(0,150,150)
    boot.append(np.linalg.lstsq(X[ix],Y[ix],rcond=None)[0])
print('ROW_IID_BOOT_95',np.quantile(boot,[.025,.975],axis=0))
print('e44_ep_stats',np.mean(e44),np.mean(ep),np.std(e44),np.std(ep),'cov',np.cov(e44,ep)[0,1])
seenrows=pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f'data/{f}.csv') for f in ('h3_shear_clamped','hm_shear_clamped','k44_cofree_clamped')])
sc=[parse_comp(s) for s in seenrows.comp]
ep_s=seenrows.Kp.values-np.array([pr(c,'Kp',1) for c in sc])
eA_s=(seenrows.K44-seenrows.Kp).values-np.array([pr(c,'A',1) for c in sc])
SP,SA=1.2*np.std(ep_s),1.2*np.std(eA_s)
print('SP_SA',SP,SA)
S=np.random.default_rng(0).choice([-1,1],(4000,150)).astype(float)
def fastjudge(y44,yp):
    er=(y44-yp)-P['A'][0]; eb=(y44-yp)-P['A'][1]
    gain=1-rm(er)/rm(eb); d=eb**2-er**2
    p=(np.count_nonzero(S@d>=d.sum())+1)/4001
    r=np.corrcoef(y44-P['K44'][0],yp-P['Kp'][0])[0,1]
    k,b=np.linalg.lstsq(np.c_[T,yp-P['Kp'][0]],y44-P['K44'][1],rcond=None)[0]
    return np.array([gain>=.1 and p<.005,r>=.5,.7<=k<=1.3 and .7<=b<=1.3]),(gain,p,r,k,b)

for truth in (0,1):

        gates.append(fastjudge(yy44,yyp)[0])
    gates=np.array(gates)
    print('STRESS_NULL',label,'all',np.all(gates,axis=1).sum(),'each',gates.sum(axis=0))
for id in ['9cfc8edaf0','c2eff007ad','b86e0d8a40']:

tk=set(map(key,t.comp))

    d=pd.read_csv(f'data/{f}.csv'); col='comp_actual' if 'comp_actual' in d else 'comp'
    print('OVERLAP',f,len(tk & set(map(key,d[col]))))
for label,mask in [('cofree',t.co.values==0),('co',t.co.values>0)]:
    print('SUBGROUP',label,'n',mask.sum(),'A',test((y44-yp)[mask],P['A'][0][mask],P['A'][1][mask]),
        'corr',np.corrcoef(e44[mask],ep[mask])[0,1],'fit',np.linalg.lstsq(X[mask],Y[mask],rcond=None)[0],
        'plain44',test(y44[mask],P['K44'][0][mask],P['K44'][1][mask]))
print('GRID',len(pd.read_csv('data/binary_kgrid.csv')),'query_dlnV_range',
 min(np.log(ctx.vegard(c)/ctx.pair[(a,b)]['V']) for _,c in comps for a,b,_,_ in ctx.pairs(c)),
 max(np.log(ctx.vegard(c)/ctx.pair[(a,b)]['V']) for _,c in comps for a,b,_,_ in ctx.pairs(c)))
times=pd.to_datetime(t.time); dd=times.diff().dt.total_seconds().dropna()
print('TIMING', (times.max()-times.min()).total_seconds(), 'median_sec',dd.median(),'mean_sec',dd.mean())

"""Crossed seed test: hm alloys at seeds 1, 2 with the k_shear_transfer protocol (xy shear, xx-yy tetragonal),
plus the yz and zx shear of the seed-0 cell. Writes scratchpad/crossed.csv, restartable."""
import os, sys, time
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(r"C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science")
os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"] = "medium-omat-0"
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
import torch; torch.set_num_threads(4)
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from ase.build import bulk
from harness import compute
from harness.compute import GPA
from harness.context import context
from harness.features import parse_comp
ctx = context(); calc = compute.calculator()
AMPS = np.array([-0.01, -0.005, 0.0, 0.005, 0.01])
OUT = Path(__file__).with_name("crossed.csv")
def e_str(atoms, v, F):
    a = atoms.copy(); a.set_cell(a.cell * (v*len(a)/a.get_volume())**(1/3), scale_atoms=True)
    a.set_cell(a.cell @ F.T, scale_atoms=True); a.calc = calc
    return a.get_potential_energy()/len(a)
def F_of(name, s):
    F = np.eye(3)
    if name == "K44": F[0,1] = s
    elif name == "K44yz": F[1,2] = s
    elif name == "K44zx": F[2,0] = s
    else: F = np.diag([np.exp(s), np.exp(-s), 1.0])
    return F
def curv(alloy, x, v, names):
    pures = {el: bulk(el, "fcc", a=4.0, cubic=True) for el in x}; out = {}
    for n in names:
        em = [e_str(alloy, v, F_of(n, s)) - sum(xi*e_str(pures[el], v, F_of(n, s)) for el, xi in x.items()) for s in AMPS]
        c2 = np.polyfit(AMPS, em, 2)[0]
        out[n] = (c2/2 if n == "Kp" else 2*c2)/v*GPA
    return out
hm = pd.read_csv(ROOT/"data/hm_shear_clamped.csv")
NMAX = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 30
done = set(map(tuple, pd.read_csv(OUT)[["comp","seed"]].astype(str).values)) if OUT.exists() else set()
t0 = time.time()
for s in hm.comp[:NMAX]:
    c = parse_comp(s); v = ctx.vegard(c)
    for seed, names in ((0, ("K44yz","K44zx")), (1, ("K44","Kp")), (2, ("K44","Kp"))):
        if (s, str(seed)) in done: continue
        al = compute.solid_solution(c, "fcc", reps=3, seed=seed); x = compute.actual_fractions(al)
        r = {"comp": s, "seed": seed, **curv(al, x, v, names)}
        pd.DataFrame([r]).to_csv(OUT, mode="a", header=not OUT.exists(), index=False)
    print(s, f"{time.time()-t0:.0f}s", flush=True)

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline
from harness.context import context
from harness.features import parse_comp
ctx = context()
kg = pd.read_csv(ROOT/"data/binary_kgrid.csv")
def splines(df):
    g = df.groupby(["pair","dlnV"])[["K44","Kp"]].mean().reset_index()
    return {(tuple(k.split("-")), ch): CubicSpline(s.dlnV, s[ch]) for k, s in g.groupby("pair") for ch in ("K44","Kp")}
S = {b: splines(kg[kg.seed==b]) for b in (0,1,2)}
cr = pd.read_csv(Path(__file__).with_name("crossed.csv"), header=0, names=["comp","seed","a","b"]); cr["K44yz"]=cr.a; cr["K44zx"]=cr.b; cr["K44"]=cr.a; cr["Kp"]=cr.b
hm = pd.read_csv(ROOT/"data/hm_shear_clamped.csv").set_index("comp")
s0 = cr[cr.seed==0].set_index("comp")
comps_all = [c for c in hm.index if all(((c, s) in set(zip(cr.comp, cr.seed))) for s in (0,1,2))]
print("complete alloys:", len(comps_all))
Y = {}
for ch in ("K44","Kp"):
    Y[(ch,0)] = hm.loc[comps_all, ch].values
    for t in (1,2):
        Y[(ch,t)] = cr[cr.seed==t].set_index("comp").loc[comps_all, ch].values
cs = [parse_comp(s) for s in comps_all]
rm = lambda e: float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.square(e))))
for ch in ("K44","Kp"):
    R = {b: np.array([sum(4*xa*xb*float(S[b][((a,bb),ch)](np.log(ctx.vegard(c)/ctx.pair[(a,bb)]["V"]))) for a,bb,xa,xb in ctx.pairs(c)) for c in cs]) for b in (0,1,2)}
    print(f"{ch}: RMSE(target seed t - rule from binary seed b), rows t, cols b")
    M = np.array([[rm(Y[(ch,t)]-R[b]) for b in (0,1,2)] for t in (0,1,2)])
    print(np.round(M,2))
    print(f"  diagonal mean {np.mean(np.diag(M)):.2f}, off-diagonal mean {np.mean(M[~np.eye(3,dtype=bool)]):.2f}")
    # same-seed covariance of the configurational parts: target offset vs binary offset relative to the 3-seed means
    ybar = np.mean([Y[(ch,t)] for t in (0,1,2)],0); rbar = np.mean([R[b] for b in (0,1,2)],0)
    same = [np.corrcoef(Y[(ch,s)]-ybar, R[s]-rbar)[0,1] for s in (0,1,2)]
    cross = [np.corrcoef(Y[(ch,t)]-ybar, R[b]-rbar)[0,1] for t in (0,1,2) for b in (0,1,2) if t!=b]
    print(f"  corr(target seed offset, binary seed offset): same seed {np.round(same,2)}, other seeds mean {np.mean(cross):+.2f}")
    print(f"  target seed sd (single cell, single plane): {np.sqrt(np.mean(np.var([Y[(ch,t)] for t in (0,1,2)],0,ddof=1))):.2f} GPa")
pl = s0.loc[comps_all]
planes = np.vstack([hm.loc[comps_all,"K44"].values, pl.K44yz.values, pl.K44zx.values])
print(f"K44 plane sd within one cell (xy,yz,zx): {np.sqrt(np.mean(np.var(planes,0,ddof=1))):.2f} GPa; 3-plane mean vs xy rms diff {rm(planes.mean(0)-planes[0]):.2f}")

.orchestra\swarm\S3\floor\opus.md:26: "prediction": "On the 104 frozen blind k_aniso_fresh alloys, with coefficients fixed at 2.8 (K44) and 1.9 (K') and no intercept: RMSE(e44 - 2.8 f) <= 0.9 RMSE(e44) and RMSE(e' - 1.9 f) <= 0.9 RMSE(e'), sign-flip p < 0.005 in both. Power 0.87, false pass 0.00 (300 simulations, noise = seen residual after f, 1.99 / 1.57 GPa).",
.orchestra\swarm\S3\floor\opus.md:27: "test": "When k_aniso_fresh.py finishes, join data/k_aniso_fresh_clamped.csv on comp with blind_frozen.csv (frozen 00:33:58, sha256 735eb7d5...0155). e = K - sum 4 x_i x_j K_ij(V0) from binary_kgrid. Use test() from scripts/k_shear_transfer.py. To register, port scratchpad/floor/pmix2.py: one MACE stress per alloy plus pures at V0; binary pressure from the derivative of the binary_vgrid spline.",
.orchestra\swarm\S3\floor\opus.md:43: "evidence": "data/binary_kgrid.csv, 3 seeds per point. Seed sd at |dlnV| < 0.11: K44 1.43 GPa, K' 0.77. At larger |dlnV|: 2.19 vs 1.37. Seed deviations are uncorrelated between channels (r -0.02), so the noise is not the floor. Every target script (k_shear_transfer.py, k44_cofree.py, k_aniso_fresh.py) uses solid_solution(..., seed=0) only, while the rule uses 3-seed binary means. Within a composition, seed deviations of the mixing pressure anticorrelate with K' deviations (r -0.56, slope -1.5), the opposite sign to the across-alloy +1.9, so a per-cell f also carries noise.",
.orchestra\swarm\S3\cobalt\opus.md:29: "test": "Script modelled on scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py: rebuild each Co cell with compute.solid_solution(c, 'fcc', 3, seed=100), set every Co symbol to M in {Ni, Rh, Cu}, keep merged compositions and drop the few that become binaries. Run kst.curvatures at the new Vegard volume, plus E_mix at V0 exp(+-0.03) for the non-pair pressure. Score each arm with its own pair rule (k_shear_transfer.test, refit k) and bootstrap the paired k difference by cell. Register before any swapped cell exists; check power with harness/power.py using the seen K44 rule rms (3.4 GPa with Co, 2.3 without).",

2. **Null, fiziksel ortak terim ile ortak hücre gürültüsünü ayıramıyor.** [scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py:94](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py:94>) — Simülasyonun alternatifinde
   \(y'=rule'+u,\ y_{44}=rule_{44}+u+\eta\).
   Buradaki \(u\), bütünüyle sıfır ortalamalı hücre gürültüsü olabilir; fiziksel ortak terim gerekmez. Koddaki σ değerlerini yeniden hesapladım: **2,24876 ve 1,93515 GPa**. Bu “yalnız ortak gürültü” modelinde bağımsız simülasyon **300/300 PASS** verdi. Kayıtlı null ise her iki kanalda hacim transferini kaldırıyor: **0/300 PASS**. Dolayısıyla `false_pass=0`, **ortak tabanın fiziksel olduğu yorumunu korumuyor**; yalnız seçilen null’u reddediyor.

3. **Eski hedef–girdi seed sızıntısı giderilmiş; konfigürasyon genellemesi hâlâ sınanmıyor.** [scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py:120](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py:120>), [harness/compute.py:56](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/harness/compute.py:56>) — İkililer 0–2, hedefler 100 kullanıyor; fakat **150 hedefin tamamı aynı permütasyon alanını**, iki kanal da aynı hücreyi kullanıyor. Satır bazlı p, farklı hedef konfigürasyonlarında tekrarlanabilirliği göstermiyor. Bununla birlikte mevcut iki-seed verisi, sonucun tamamen hücre gürültüsü olmasına karşı kanıt taşıyor: [data/k_aniso_fresh_clamped.csv:2](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/data/k_aniso_fresh_clamped.csv:2>) ile eşleşen **45 kompozisyonda**, kanal farklarının seed-değişimi korelasyonu **0,316**; çapraz-seed artık korelasyonları **0,689 ve 0,821**. Ortak katkının önemli bölümü seed değişince korunuyor. Bunlar yalnız iki ortak seed ve 45 kompozisyon olduğundan kesin ayrıştırma sağlamıyor.

4. **Joint fit bağımsız bir üçüncü doğrulama değil; fakat otomatik PASS da değil.** [scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py:78](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/scripts/k_aniso_fresh.py:78>) — \(\delta_A=e_{44}-e'\) tanımıyla
   \(K_{44}-pair_{44}=T_{44}+e'+\delta_A\).
   Böylece A artığının açıklayıcılarla küçük izdüşümü zaten k ve b’yi 1’e yaklaştırıyor. Üstelik `e'`, hedef hücrenin ölçülmüş K′ değerini içeriyor; bu bağımsız K44 tahmini değil. Yine de kriter bozuk/tekil değil: tasarım matrisinin koşul sayısı **1,41**. Gerçek k=0 koyduğum kontrolde A kapısı **300/300 geçerken**, joint kapısı **0/300 geçti**. Mevcut 45 kompozisyonda K44(seed100) ile e′(seed0) kullanınca **k=0,663**, b=1,001 çıkıyor; küçük ve keşifsel bu alt küme tam sonucu çürütmez, fakat bağımsız-hücre kontrolünün önemini gösterir.

5. **Sonradan eşik değişikliği bulmadım; “150 yeni kompozisyon” ifadesi tam doğru değil.** [claims/claims.jsonl:69](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/claims/claims.jsonl:69>), [claims/claims.jsonl:72](<C:/Users/can02/Projects/AI driven Science/claims/claims.jsonl:72>) — Eski/yeni kayıtların eşikleri aynı. Yeni kayıt **00:15:47**, ilk seed100 hedefi **00:16:04**. Script hash’i ön kayıt, sonuç ve mevcut dosyada **e6d0c50bb4d32dc8**; iki sonuç-veri hash’i de eşleşiyor. Ancak eski geri çekilmiş dosyayla **45/150 kompozisyon örtüşüyor**; defter 44 diyor. Diğer altı dışlama kümesiyle atom-sayısı düzeyinde örtüşme **0**. Bu 45’i çıkarınca kalan **105 hedef yine geçiyor**: kazanç **%46,70**, r=**0,7443**, k=**0,9522**, b=**0,8759**. Örtüşme PASS’ın nedeni görünmüyor. İçe aktarılan yardımcı kod ön kayıtta hash’lenmediğinden bütün hesap zincirinin değişmezliği ayrıca kanıtlanmış değil.

**En büyük şüpheyi çözecek tek ek test:** Aynı 150 kompozisyonun her biri için, **hücreler arasında da benzersiz iki yeni seed** kullanarak iki kanalı hesapla. Önceden tanımlanmış analizde aynı-hücre ve çapraz-hücre artık kovaryansını karşılaştır; joint fit’i karşı hücrenin e′ değeriyle değerlendir. Güç null’u A transferini koruyup ortaklığı yalnız hücre gürültüsünden üretmeli. Böylece gürültü ortaklığı ile kompozisyona bağlı ortak katkı ayrılır.

**Maliyet:** 300 yeni hücre, mevcut protokolle **14.660 enerji değerlendirmesi**. Mevcut zaman damgaları aynı cihaz/duty için yaklaşık **90 dakika duvar süresi** öngörüyor. **CPU-only maliyeti ölçülmemiş:** hesaplayıcı CUDA varsa GPU seçiyor; bu süreyi CPU-saat diye sunamam. Hiçbir dosyayı değiştirmedim.
